label: Free 2.0
title: Marking layers and Content Credentials
lede: Witness 2.0 records and checks the marking layers the final Code of Practice asks for, and shows Content Credentials in the browser. Everything is MIT and a drop-in for 1.x markings, with Node 22 as the new minimum.

items.title: Record which layers mark your content
items.text: Markings now carry a schema version and a list of layers (visible, metadata, watermark, credentials), so you can document which techniques you apply. Old markings stay readable.

items.title: Check against the two-layer expectation
items.text: assessLayers tells you whether audio, image and video content reaches the two machine-readable techniques the Code of Practice asks for, and what is missing. inspectLayers reads the layers straight from a file.

items.title: Gate your build with witness layers
items.text: The CLI lists the layers of each file and, with --require, exits 1 when a file has fewer machine-readable layers than the Code asks for. Use --assume for a watermark your provider applies and Witness cannot see.
items.code:
npx witness layers ./out/*.png --require
npx witness layers ./out/*.png --assume watermark --require
items.outputTitle: Real output (first run exits 1, second exits 0)
items.output:
out/plain.png: image, layers metadata, 1 of 2 machine-readable, missing e.g. watermark or credentials
out/plain.png: image, layers metadata + watermark, 2 of 2 machine-readable

items.title: Show Content Credentials in the browser
items.text: The new <witness-credentials> element reads the C2PA manifest of an image, audio or video file client-side and shows who made it and whether it declares AI. It reads the manifest but does not verify the signature, and says so.
items.codeTitle: HTML (element) and readC2pa (same reader, in Node)
items.code:
<script type="module">
  import "@sweberdev/witness/elements";
</script>

<witness-credentials src="/media/picture.jpg"></witness-credentials>

// Node, same reader:
readC2pa(bytes);
items.outputTitle: Real readC2pa output on the package's test fixture (trimmed)
items.output:
{
  aiGenerated: true,
  sourceType: 'trainedAlgorithmicMedia',
  generator: 'Image Model X 3',
  verified: false,
  claimGenerator: 'Witness test generator 1.0',
  actions: [ 'c2pa.created' ]
}

note: Outputs were produced by running @sweberdev/witness 2.0.0 from npm. The credentials example uses a test fixture, and the output was reduced to selected fields.
